speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, have you noticed if the sensation of spinning is triggered specifically when you move your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical picture of a sudden, brief (3 minutes) episode of vertigo triggered by a head position change (going to bed), followed by complete resolution and no other neurological deficits, is classic for BPPV. I will proceed with the Epley maneuver.
